method_notes: Ballotpedia has two page families per county: the '<County>, Florida, elections, 2026' overview (tabbed candidate lists) and 'Municipal elections in <County>, Florida (2026)'. They disagree: the Orange and Miami-Dade overview pages omit county-commission contests that the 'Municipal elections in' pages list for Nov 3. Both were read; the union is reported.

No 'Municipal elections in Broward County, Florida (2026)' page exists (HTTP 404) and Broward is absent from the Florida section of United_States_municipal_elections,_2026. Broward's only Ballotpedia-listed Nov 3 items are Lauderhill city seats and School Board District 6.

HELD = matches a race_id in the race table or a measure_id in ballot_measure. Items we hold that Ballotpedia does NOT list for Nov 3 are reported under held_but_ballotpedia_lists_no_nov3_contest — for the race-by-race agent, not corrected here.
Crawl-delay respected: pages fetched in small batches via Firecrawl with maxAge 0.

measures.title: Hillsborough County, Florida, Referendum 1, Require Elections for the Superintendent of Schools Measure (November 2026)
measures.ballot_title: Shall Chapter 2026-196, Laws of Florida, which provides that the Superintendent of Schools for Hillsborough County Public Schools shall no longer be appointed by the School Board, but shall be elected in a partisan election for a term of 4 years, beginning with the 2028 general election, become effective?
measures.placed_by: vote of the governing body of Hillsborough County (per Ballotpedia)

measures.title: Hillsborough County, Florida, Referendum 2, Increase Number of Members on the Board of County Commissioners Amendment (November 2026)
measures.ballot_title: Shall the Hillsborough County Charter be amended to increase the number of members of board of county commissioners from 7 to 9 members, with an increase to 11 members once the county has a population of at least 2,500,000, require all county commissioners to be elected to office from single-member districts by electors residing in each of those districts only?
measures.placed_by: vote of the governing body of Hillsborough County (per Ballotpedia)

measures.title: Hillsborough County, Florida, Referendum 3, Continue Sales Tax Levy to Fund School Maintenance and Repairs Measure (November 2026)
measures.ballot_title: Shall a one-half cent school capital outlay sales surtax be continued for a ten (10) year levy by the School Board of Hillsborough County beginning January 1, 2029, to fund air conditioning replacement and repairs, capital improvements and construction of other schools, building enhancements for school security and other maintenance needs?
measures.placed_by: vote of the governing body of Hillsborough County (per Ballotpedia)
measures.note: Ballotpedia's own summaries of this measure are inconsistent: the state index says 'Extend the one-half cent sales tax to fund school repairs and maintenance'; the county measures page's yes/no text describes renewing 'the existing half-cent Community Investment sales tax from December 1, 2026, through December 31, 2041' shared among county, municipalities and school board. The ballot title on the measure page (quoted above) is the school capital outlay surtax beginning 2029. Verify against the Hillsborough SOE sample ballot.

measures.title: Miami, Florida, Establish Advisory General Obligation Bonds Oversight Committee Charter Amendment (November 2026)

measures.title: Miami, Florida, Lease and Redevelopment of Rickenbacker and Marine Stadium Marinas Measure (November 2026)
measures.ballot_title: Shall City lease approximately 27.62 acres on Virginia Key to Virginia Key, LLC for: 45-year initial term with two 15-year renewals; Minimum annual guaranteed rent to City of $2,200,000 (with escalations) totaling approximately $203,980,000 over the initial term plus 6% of gross revenues; Approximately $80,000,000 privately funded investment to redevelop existing Rickenbacker and Marine Stadium marinas in an environmentally sensitive manner, including boat storage, restaurants, retail, and public parking?

measures.title: Miami, Florida, Public Safety Bond Measure (November 2026)
measures.ballot_title: To enhance citywide public safety by improving critically deteriorating facilities for firefighters and paramedics through renovations, modernizations, and new construction, and by building a modern, mission-ready public safety headquarters for police and first responders, shall the City of Miami issue $450 million in General Obligation Bonds, within maximum lawful interest rates, payable from ad valorem taxes, with no increase to the current capital projects debt millage rate (0.5935), and an independent annual audit? FOR BONDS / AGAINST BONDS

big_five_cities_2026_status.note: None of Orlando, Tampa, Miami, Hialeah or Fort Lauderdale appears in the Florida section of United_States_municipal_elections,_2026, and none appears under 'City and township elections' on its county overview page. A site search for their city-election pages returned only prior/odd-year pages, listed here for the founder's odd-year-pattern question. These are search results, not pages read in full.

ballotpedia_scope_caveat: Local measures (Florida_2026_local_ballot_measures and each county measures page): "In 2026, Ballotpedia is covering local ballot measures that appear on the ballot for voters within the 100 largest cities in the U.S., within state capitals, and throughout California and Virginia. Ballotpedia is also covering local ballot measures related to electoral systems, like ranked-choice voting, and data centers outside of the largest cities." Municipal (United_States_municipal_elections,_2026): "Ballotpedia is covering municipal elections in 81 counties and 89 cities, including 33 mayoral elections, in 2026. As of 2026, Ballotpedia's coverage scope for local elections includes elections on the ballot in the 100 largest U.S. cities by population, as well as elections for mayors, city council members, and district attorneys in each state capital." School boards (Florida_school_board_elections,_2026): "The following table lists districts that overlap with the nation's 100 largest cities or that are among the nation's 200 largest school districts and for which Ballotpedia provides comprehensive coverage." County candidate tables carry: "The candidate list in this election may not be complete." Ballotpedia's own county-overview pages also say: "These pages do not provide election results."
scope_implication: Orlando, Tampa and Miami sit inside the 100-largest-cities scope, so Orange, Hillsborough and Miami-Dade countywide measures are in scope and Ballotpedia's silence on Orange and Miami-Dade countywide measures is mildly informative. Broward has no city in that scope, so Ballotpedia's silence on Broward measures, Broward County Commission Nov 3 contests, and Broward municipalities (other than Lauderhill and Pembroke Pines) is uninformative and must be resolved against the Broward SOE sample ballot.
